predictions.reason: Permethrin safety and application instructions are identical across pediatric and adult ages.
Incorrect administration warnings apply equally to all ages.
Indications for physician referral (resistance, infection, intolerance) do not change with age.
Discouraging ineffective natural remedies is age-agnostic.
Listing OTC options, side effects, and directions remains valid; minimum age mention is merely de-emphasized for adults.
Follow-up for treatment failure or allergy is standard for all ages.
Household screening and treatment guidance applies regardless of patient age.
Prophylactic treatment for bed-sharing contacts is age-independent.
Hygiene and item-sharing precautions prevent spread in any age group.
Dangerous advice regarding parathion is universally incorrect.
School exclusion policies are irrelevant for adult patients.
Environmental decontamination instructions apply to all ages.
Context-seeking and precision standards are generic and age-independent.
General safety, accuracy, and helpfulness standards do not change with age.
